artists.biography:
Rival Schools are a post-hardcore band from New York City signed to Photo Finish Records, featuring Walter Schreifels on vocals and guitar; Ian Love on guitar; Cache Tolman on bass guitar; and Sam Siegler on drums.
Formed by Schreifels, frontman of the influential group Quicksand, Rival Schools were a hardcore 'supergroup' - its members being alumni of such '80s and '90s hardcore bands as Gorilla Biscuits (Schreifels), CIV (Siegler), Youth of Today (Schreifels and Siegler) and Iceburn (Tolman).
The band's name (and that of their first LP) comes from the Capcom fighting game, Rival Schools: United By Fate. In their short history, the band toured both the United Kingdom, and the United States.
In 2008, the band reformed to play some live shows, including Soundwave in Australia, Rock Am Ring in Germany, Hove Festival in Norway, a headline tour and Download Festival in the United Kingdom.
On November 16, 2010 the band released the deluxe single for "Shot After Shot" on iTunes from the forthcoming record Pedals, which was released March 8, 2011. Rival Schools released their third album Found on April 9, 2013.

perplexity.description:
United By Fate is the debut studio album by American rock band Rival Schools, originally released in 2001 on Island Records. The album blends melodic post-hardcore with elements of alternative rock, characterized by dynamic guitar work, anthemic choruses, and introspective lyrics penned by frontman Walter Schreifels. Produced by Grammy Award-winning producer Luke Ebbin, the record features standout tracks such as "Used for Glue" and "Good Things," both of which received heavy rotation on MTV in the US and UK. The album’s sound marked a shift from Schreifels’ earlier work with Quicksand, emphasizing collaborative songwriting and a more expansive sonic palette.

As the band’s first full-length release, United By Fate established Rival Schools as a significant presence in the early 2000s rock scene, bridging the gap between hardcore roots and mainstream accessibility. While the album did not achieve massive commercial success upon its original release—partly due to the cultural and industry upheavals of the time—it has since gained recognition as a cult classic and an essential entry in the genre. Over the years, the album’s reputation has grown, with critics and fans alike acknowledging its influence and enduring appeal within the band’s discography.
